annotations.text:
A · Open the device (recommended)
The signature interaction IS the argument: the real product opens into the six layers AID-IoT makes. One component reused on Product, Software and Services pages.
World: cool off-white ground, committed orange fields, ink, Geist + JetBrains Mono.
Risk: needs 3D models (reference models until CAD arrives) and an R3F engineer. Mobile: lower-LOD model or 60-frame sequence.

B · Panel room
The site speaks control-room mimic-diagram grammar a non-engineer can read; one diagram component draws every operation. Warm paper + ink, one live colour, Archivo + Archivo Narrow.
Risk: can read as an HMI rather than a pitch; ~20 diagrams to draw. Cheapest to run (SVG only).

C · Field log
Editorial, documentary photography; paper → Signal before/after as the recurring device. Bodoni Moda + Public Sans; palette from the photographs.
Risk: lives on a real photo shoot (or generated environments with the §09 prefix for launch); weakest at showing software without recorded dashboards.

How to read these boards
Each is a first viewport + the signature interaction as three scroll stops + the four story beats. Fidelity is deliberately 'direction', not final: judge the idea, the world and the voice, not the pixel polish.
All three keep the mark, the five-branch nav, the proof strip and 'Talk to an engineer'.
